evidence: Enumerated all 51 scored criteria (functional 41, polish 5, visual 5) plus 2 gates and checked every plausible overlapping pair. The task explicitly partitions shared observables with ownership clauses: hro_arrive_bottom 'Arrival of several cards together belongs to hro_bulk_move'; hro_interview_full 'Overfill by a multi-card move belongs to hro_bulk_places and by undo to hro_undo_full'; hro_undo_restores 'The A2 undo in B(12) is graded only in hro_undo_conflict' (repeated-undo refusal in B(5) owned by hro_undo_once); hro_drafts 'Clearing the box after sending is graded in hro_msg_compose'; hro_candidate_view 'Whether other people's applications appear is graded only in hro_candidate_private; a candidate's reply is graded in hro_msg_exchange'; hro_candidate_linked 'This row alone owns that link; rows run on his seeded conversation instead are not reduced for it'; functional prompt.md:19 'an Activity line added by a refused action is deducted only in hro_activity_refusals'; hro_pol_live_thread 'This row owns the draft and focus; where the view goes while reading earlier messages is graded in Functional'; hro_pol_failed_send 'Unsaved note drafts are graded only in hro_pol_session_resume'. Cross-dimension splits are clean: hro_thread_earlier (30-per-page count/order) vs hro_pol_earlier_place (anchor position, rules 6 'must not move what the reader was looking at'); hro_unread_scrolled_up (place while scrolled up) vs hro_pol_live_thread (at-newest draft/focus/view); hro_drafts (switch/reload) vs hro_pol_session_resume (ended session, other user on same browser); hro_live_board (move/new card appears) vs hro_pol_live_board (details/note/focus/scroll preserved). Role rows are split by actor and action: hro_mgr_late_stages / hro_mgr_early_refused (Ingrid on J1, incl. open-job/add-candidate) / hro_mgr_other_job (Bill move) / hro_notes (Bill note) / hro_observer_readonly / hro_candidate_no_staff (writes) / hro_candidate_private (reads) / hro_anonymous (401) / hro_thread_access (send replays in Aud, Ingrid, Noor sessions). Single-skip (hro_move_one_stage), bulk-skip atomicity (hro_bulk_all_or_none) and stale refusal (hro_stale_refused) use different requests and are separable: an app validating single moves but not the bulk endpoint fails only hro_bulk_all_or_none. No incompatible demands found: arrival-at-bottom, board-order bulk arrival (rules 3 'by stage in the order listed above, then by place'), undo-to-original-place, single-level undo, note-does-not-block-undo, seen semantics (Observer never counts; J2 manager Bill counts) and candidate wording are mutually consistent across criteria and with hireops_rules.md. Attempted counterexamples: (a) a broken app with no capacity check loses hro_interview_full, hro_bulk_places and hro_undo_full, but these are three distinct request paths (single move, multi-card move, undo) explicitly partitioned, and a partially correct app separates them; (b) a conforming app that refuses only in the UI passes hro_refused_put_back ('A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes') while failing hro_interview_full on replay, so neither row subsumes the other; (c) a conforming alternative that stores drafts server-side or in localStorage keyed by user passes both hro_drafts and hro_pol_session_resume - no incompatible product. Observations kept as Note-level, not defects: several rows require a success of another feature as their positive control/precondition (hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread are 0 when no live update arrives, overlapping the evidence of hro_live_board / hro_msg_exchange; hro_refused_put_back needs a server refusal that hro_interview_full grades; candidate own-data load is the control in hro_candidate_view, hro_candidate_private and hro_candidate_no_staff; hro_job_open accepts 'the places limit in L' and 'the manager's own moves in R' as alternative evidence when places/manager are not displayed). These are mandated by REVIEW_POLICY 'A negative needs a successful control ... A dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing' and the template 'If one cannot be performed, the criterion fails'; the graded observable differs in each pair. Their concentration on the live-update and candidate-load preconditions is a discrimination concern for check 40, not a row-28 duplication. Minor wording tension: functional prompt.md:23 and polish prompt 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' coexist with these precondition zeros; the criterion texts themselves state the zero explicitly ('this row is 0; say so', 'makes this row 0'), so the targeted outcome is unambiguous. This is a static source review; no configured judge run measured how the judge applies these couplings, which row 28 does not require.
